message:
QUESTION:
Under company policy, which of the five stores should receive this year's refurbishment budget?

DATA:
Five-store retail chain, financial year 2025. A refurbishment budget is available for one store. Company policy: the budget goes to the store with the lowest annual sales per square foot of sales floor (the company's space-productivity KPI), measured on a full-year basis.

| Store | Annual sales 2025 | Sales floor area (sq ft) | Gross internal area incl. stockrooms (sq ft) |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | 10,000 |
| South | £3.6m | 15,000 | 18,000 |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| West | £2.1m | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | 14,000 |

Annual sales 2024: North £2.3m, South £3.5m, East £1.7m, West £2.9m, Central £4.0m. Floor areas were the same in 2024.

Operations note: West was closed from January to March 2025 (3 months) for flood repairs, so its 2025 sales cover 9 trading months. All other stores traded for all 12 months in both years. The flood repairs were covered by insurance and did not change the store's layout.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [method] The company KPI is sales per square foot of sales floor, not gross internal area. Using gross area changes the densities and their relative gaps. CORRECTION: Sales-floor densities (2025 as reported): North £300, South £240, East £300, West £210, Central £350.
F2. [calculation] £4.2m / 14,000 = £300, not £320 (even on the draft's gross-area basis). CORRECTION: £300 per sq ft gross (or £350 on sales floor). Central is 50%, not 'roughly 60%', above South and East on gross area.
F3. [omission] Ignores that West traded for only 9 months in 2025 (flood closure), while policy requires a full-year basis. CORRECTION: Annualised West sales = £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m: £280 per sq ft of sales floor. The lowest full-year density is South at £240, so South gets the budget.
F4. [misreport] In 2024 West had the second-highest density (£2.9m / 10,000 = £290 per sq ft of sales floor). South was the weakest (£3.5m / 15,000 = £233). CORRECTION: West was not weak in 2024. Its 2025 'decline' is the closure, so there is no trend case for West; South was weakest in both years.

EXTENSIONS:
- Show the decision is robust: South is lowest on sales-floor density in both 2024 (£233) and annualised 2025 (£240), while on gross area South and East tie at £200 once West is annualised (£233), which shows why the KPI's definition matters.
- Check West's post-reopening run rate (monthly sales April-December vs the same months of 2024) to confirm that annualising is fair, i.e. that West did not reopen with depressed trade.
- Consider return on refurbishment rather than lowest density alone: e.g. South's large floor (15,000 sq ft) means each £10/sq ft uplift is worth £150,000 a year, more than in any other store.

FINAL VERSION:
# Refurbishment Budget: Store Productivity Review, FY2025

## Recommendation

**Under company policy, the refurbishment budget should go to South.** On a full-year basis, South has the lowest sales per square foot of sales floor, at **£240**. West, which the draft recommended, is at **£280** once its sales are annualised. Its low raw figure comes from the three-month flood closure, not from weak trading.

## What changed from the draft

The draft broke the policy in two ways, and both affect the answer:

1. **Wrong denominator.** The policy KPI is sales per square foot of **sales floor**. The draft used gross internal area, which includes stockrooms. Sales per sq ft of gross internal area may be a useful secondary measure of how efficiently the whole building is used, but it is not the policy test.
2. **No full-year adjustment.** The policy says the KPI is measured on a full-year basis. West traded for only 9 months in 2025, so its £2.1m cannot be compared directly with the other stores' 12-month figures.

These errors led to two false claims in the draft:

- West's "drop of more than a quarter" (£2.9m to £2.1m, −27.6%) is mostly the closure.
- West was not the weakest store in 2024. South was.

## Sales density on sales floor area, 2025

West's sales are annualised as £2.1m ÷ 9 × 12 = **£2.8m**.

| Rank | Store | 2025 sales (full-year basis) | Sales floor (sq ft) | Sales per sq ft |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | £350 |
| 2= | North | £2.4m | 8,000 | £300 |
| 2= | East | £1.8m | 6,000 | £300 |
| 4 | West | £2.8m *(annualised)* | 10,000 | £280 |
| **5 (lowest)** | **South** | **£3.6m** | **15,000** | **£240** |

The annualisation decides the result. West's unadjusted figure would be £2.1m ÷ 10,000 = £210, which would wrongly make it the lowest.

## Robustness checks

- **Seasonality.** Pro-rating assumes January to March is an average quarter, worth 25% of annual sales. For West to fall below South's £240, its full-year sales would need to be under £2.4m. Since April to December brought in £2.1m, January to March would have to normally bring in less than £0.3m, which is under 12.5% of the year. That is implausibly weak, even for a soft post-Christmas quarter. West's 2024 monthly sales, if available, would confirm this, but the conclusion is very unlikely to change.
- **Prior year.** In 2024 every store traded a full year with the same floor areas, so no adjustment is needed. The 2024 densities give the same answer:

| Rank | Store | 2024 sales | Sales per sq ft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Central | £4.0m | £333 |
| 2 | West | £2.9m | £290 |
| 3 | North | £2.3m | £288 |
| 4 | East | £1.7m | £283 |
| **5 (lowest)** | **South** | **£3.5m** | **£233** |

South was the lowest in 2024 as well, so its weak productivity is persistent, not a one-year effect. West ranked second that year.

## Trends

| Store | 2024 | 2025 (full-year basis) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| North | £2.3m | £2.4m | +4.3% |
| South | £3.5m | £3.6m | +2.9% |
| East | £1.7m | £1.8m | +5.9% |
| West | £2.9m | £2.8m *(annualised)* | −3.4% |
| Central | £4.0m | £4.2m | +5.0% |

- **Chain sales.** Reported chain sales fell from £14.4m to £14.1m. On a like-for-like basis, with West annualised, the chain grew to about £14.8m (+2.8%). The reported fall is entirely due to West's closure.
- **West.** West's underlying dip of about 3% is worth watching. Its cause can't be established from annual figures. Monthly sales since reopening would show whether it reflects disruption around the closure or a continuing trend. Either way, it does not make West the weakest store under the policy.
- **South.** South is growing, but more slowly than the chain. Its problem is space productivity. It has the largest sales floor (15,000 sq ft) and sells less per foot than any other store. A refurbishment that improves layout, space use or the range could address this directly. Reconfiguring or reducing the sales floor is also worth considering.

## Next steps

1. **Allocate the FY2025 refurbishment budget to South.**
2. If available, use West's 2024 monthly sales to confirm its usual January to March share. This would fully close off the seasonality question.
3. Monitor West's trading since reopening as a separate issue from the refurbishment decision.
4. **Measure the result.** Twelve months after the works, compare South's sales per sq ft of sales floor with its pre-works level (£240). Also compare it with the rest of the chain over the same period, so that chain-wide trends are not mistaken for the effect of the refurbishment. If the store closes or trades partially during the works, use a full-year-equivalent figure, as was done for West here.
5. Schedule the works to avoid peak trading periods.
